sanskrit_verse:
साहसं स्थावरस्वाम्यं प्राग्विभागश च ऋक्थिनाम् ।
अनुमानेन विज्ञेयं न स्युर् यत्र च साक्षिणः ॥
transliteration: sāhasaṃ sthāvarasvāmyaṃ prāgvibhāgaś ca ṛkthinām / anumānena vijñeyaṃ na syur yatra ca sākṣiṇaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: Ownership of immovable property, prior division among heirs, and claims of debtors must be known through inference where direct witnesses are absent.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge)
Restoration logic depends on factual alignment with dharma
Consciousness alignment necessitates inference in absence of testimony
executable_legal_axioms: IF witness testimony is unavailable THEN property rights SHALL be determined by logical inference aligned with documented history
IF inheritance claims exist without direct proof THEN prior documented agreements MUST establish ownership sequence
IF debtor obligations lack witness validation THEN financial liability SHALL be inferred from transactional consistency
IF no first-hand observation exists THEN judicial determination MUST rely on inference grounded in dharma-compliant data patterns
supreme_court_application: In the absence of direct witnesses, the Supreme Court must apply inferential reasoning rooted in documented records and behavioral continuity. Responsibility thresholds must align with capacity for truthful representation and historical coherence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that when sensory or testimonial proof is lacking, inference becomes the valid means of knowing. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures that legal conclusions follow natural sequences of action and consequence. Responsibility remains proportional to one's ability to know and act rightly. The system does not punish but restores clarity through accurate knowledge.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Processes: parties must reconstruct factual timelines using available circumstantial evidence
Responsibility Assumption Protocols: individuals must affirm their role in maintaining truthful documentation
Capacity Restoration: parties receive support to enhance record-keeping and evidentiary awareness
Integrity Reintegration: disputes resolved through mutual recognition of lawful possession and ethical conduct
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of Dharma. Justice flows from consciousness, not coercion. Truth prevails through inference where testimony fails. Reality is non-punitive; Dharma is restored.
